documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 02/27/2025 via emergency department. Discharged: 03/04/2025.
Service: Gastroenterology.

Reason for admission: a week of steady epigastric pain boring through to the back, with vomiting, worse each day.

History: 60-year-old man with chronic calcific pancreatitis and exocrine insufficiency since 2021, type 3c diabetes on glargine, untreated chronic hepatitis C, treated distal esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (2024) and follicular lymphoma (2023), hairy cell leukemia in remission. No alcohol since 2021.
Allergies: NKDA.
Home medications: pancrelipase 36,000 units with meals and snacks; insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime.

On admission: vital signs stable (BP 128/78, HR 92, afebrile, SpO2 97%). Epigastric tenderness without rebound or guarding.
Labs: Na 140, K 4.0, Cl 108, HCO3 15, BUN 18, creatinine 1.0, glucose 90, calcium 9.2, anion gap 17. Albumin 2.7, AST 82, ALT 61, bilirubin 0.8. Hgb 11.7, WBC 6.4.
CT abdomen/pelvis 02/27: no acute pancreatitis; small amount of free fluid near the pancreatic tail.
MRCP 02/28: disruption of the main pancreatic duct in the tail with a small adjacent fluid collection, on a background of the known gland atrophy, calcification and ductal dilation.

Diagnosis: pancreatic duct leak (disruption in the tail) with small adjacent collection, in chronic pancreatitis.

Hospital course: managed without endoscopic or surgical intervention. Bowel rest, IV fluids, IV antiemetics and analgesia. Glargine continued with glucose checks; dextrose-containing fluids while NPO; no hypoglycemia. Pain and vomiting settled by day 3; diet advanced from clear liquids to low-fat solids, tolerated, with Creon. Bicarbonate 21 on the day of discharge.

Discharge medications: unchanged. Pancrelipase 36,000 units with meals and snacks; insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime.
Follow-up: primary care within 1 week with BMP. Gastroenterology clinic with repeat MRCP in about 10 weeks.
Return precautions: recurrent pain, vomiting, fever.

documents.title: Cardiac Surgery Consultation
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
CARDIAC SURGERY CONSULTATION
Date of consult: 02/23/2026

Asked to evaluate for surgery: Enterococcus faecalis aortic valve endocarditis with new first-degree AV block.

Data: blood cultures 3 of 3 positive for E. faecalis, ampicillin susceptible; cultures from 02/22 no growth to date. TTE 02/19: aortic valve vegetation, moderate AR, normal LV size and function. TEE 02/20: vegetation about 8 mm on the aortic valve, moderate AR, no abscess or other perivalvular extension. ECG: PR 260 ms (170 ms in 2024); daily ECGs since admission show no lengthening and no higher-grade block.

Background: chronic hepatitis C with hepatic dysfunction, chronic pancreatitis, type 3c diabetes, treated esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, lymphoma and hairy cell leukemia.

Assessment: the conduction change raises concern for perivalvular spread, but TEE shows none, cultures cleared within 3 days of antibiotics, the PR interval is stable, the vegetation is under 10 mm and the left ventricle is preserved.

Recommendation: medical therapy, no surgery at this time. Continue daily ECGs while inpatient; reconsult for progression of block, heart failure, embolic events or persistent bacteremia.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary — Cardiology
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 02/19/2026 via emergency department to the cardiac intensive care unit. Transferred to the cardiology ward 02/23/2026. Discharged: 03/03/2026.

Presenting problem: a week of fevers, malaise, fatigue and mild shortness of breath.

History: 61-year-old man with untreated chronic hepatitis C, chronic pancreatitis with exocrine insufficiency, type 3c diabetes on glargine, follicular lymphoma in remission, distal esophageal squamous cell carcinoma treated with chemoradiation in 2024 without recurrence, and hairy cell leukemia in remission. No alcohol since 2021.
Allergies: NKDA.
Home medications: pancrelipase 36,000 units with meals and snacks; insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime.

Admission findings: T 38.8 C (101.8 F), BP 120/72, HR 96, RR 18, SpO2 97% on room air. Early diastolic murmur along the left sternal border in full expiration. Lungs clear.
Labs: Hgb 10.2, WBC 12.2, platelets 165. Albumin 2.8. Creatinine 0.84.
ECG: sinus rhythm, first-degree AV block, PR 260 ms, new against 2024 baseline (170 ms).

Microbiology: 3 of 3 blood culture sets from 02/19 grew Enterococcus faecalis, ampicillin susceptible (reported 02/20). Repeat cultures 02/22: no growth at 5 days.
Imaging: TTE 02/19: aortic valve vegetation, moderate aortic regurgitation, normal LV size and systolic function. TEE 02/20: aortic valve vegetation approximately 8 mm, moderate regurgitation, no abscess, fistula or other perivalvular extension.

Diagnosis: infective endocarditis of the native aortic valve due to Enterococcus faecalis, complicated by new first-degree AV block.

Course: started IV ampicillin plus ceftriaxone on 02/19. Defervesced by 02/23. Monitored in the CICU on telemetry until 02/23; daily ECGs with stable PR, no progression. Cardiac surgery consulted because of the conduction change and advised medical therapy given no perivalvular extension on TEE, cultures cleared within 3 days and a stable PR. Glargine continued with point-of-care glucose; no hypoglycemia. Right arm PICC placed 03/02 for outpatient therapy.

Discharge plan:
- IV ampicillin plus ceftriaxone through home infusion, to complete 6 weeks from culture clearance on 02/22/2026: last dose 04/05/2026.
- Weekly CBC and BMP through home infusion.
- Amoxicillin 2 g by mouth 30-60 minutes before dental procedures, from now on.
- Primary care within 1 week; cardiology clinic with repeat TTE in about 10 weeks.
- Return for fever, worsening shortness of breath, palpitations, fainting, or PICC problems.
Discharge medications: as above plus home pancrelipase and glargine unchanged.
